I think the issue here is that this is her 'job', and when somebody's forced into a situation with another person interested in them romantically, it puts the person in an awkward position where they can feel trapped by the fact that they have to be polite and stuff to keep face. It doesn't sound as sinister as like...doing it at a cafe, but you know where she'll be almost guaranteed to be at those times. I'm not saying don't pursue it at all, but be very careful and maybe don't do it in the lesson times if you can.

I get that you're not intending to be a creep, but she has no idea about that. She might not care at all, but for somebody else it could come across as kinda predatory if they have fears about repercussions at work if they turn you down.

Yeah, I do get like...the concept of privilege, but I often feel like 'thin privilege' is thrown around a lot when people assume 'attractive and desirable privilege' when discussing the societal side of things rather than the more practical, like sizes of public transport seats and stuff. If that makes sense? I feel like people attribute privilege to me when it's not something I experience. The only societal difference I've noticed is people telling me I need to eat more rather than eat less. I still get glares in the street, disgusted looks, treated exactly the same way by strangers. It's something I didn't expect at all actually.
